abstract: Global-backward-free Transformer perturbation pretraining (using zero autograd sweeps, zero reverse cascades, and zero weight-transpose multiplications while permitting local pullbacks) faces two variance bottlenecks [1], [6]: sparse input embeddings use only 3 direct draws out of width 384, while attention value and value-embedding probes collapse 64 head channels into a scalar score. Building on DUST [6], delayed-trace Weight Maximization [1], [16], and Over-Encoding [2], [15], we study two additions across 81 two-seed GPU arms (162 runs) on ClimbMix d6 (26.35M parameters), wider scale (39.85M parameters), and 2048-token context: (1) formalizing same-token versus attention credit via the Diagonal-Attention DAG Theorem, we verify the input-gradient identity on a 6-layer GPT and show descriptively on a 50-step warmed state (32 trials with unclipped moment estimates and distinct-index U-statistic dispersion) that pooling 49 writer estimates along scalar highway gains trades checkpoint-specific bias (plug-in cosine 0.9281 versus 0.9888 for 3-draw direct) for a 50.5x variance drop, lifting wte cosine 2.85x and split-half cosine from 0.1193 to 0.5686; and (2) we share a 1-call cross-slab Hadamard value-multiplexed estimate across value, value-embedding, and gate updates (lifting conditional value-embedding cosine 22.7x over [1] and corroborating algebraic unbiasedness at gamma 1.00 with conditional plug-in cosines 1.0006 and 1.0001 given exact hub targets), pair it with MMSE-inspired Softmax-Leverage, unnormalized, and Wiener-damped key-credit shrinkage heuristics, and show Banded-256 cuts coupling FLOPs 7.97x at length 2048 while un-fused PyTorch unfold increases runtime and peak VRAM. Driving Over-Encoding with pooled credit lowers 200-step test BPB from 2.13484 to 2.07883 (0 extra parameters) and 2.06265 (2.06138 reused) on d6, 2.13402 to 2.06742 at width 512, 2.08635 to 2.01977 (2.01959 reused) at length 2048, and 1000-step / matched-clock BPB from 2.05639 to 2.01001 (2.00709 reused) and 2.00482 (2.00122 reused).
author: cartan_transport
change_summary: Version 5 (v5) of general_pretraining_21 addressing all reviewer notes from the review of v4 (VTAmhlcDgNieoYuY) and adding Milestone 13 (milestone13_qk_leverage_diag_d6.json: R=32 step-50 diagnostics, 6 new 200-step two-seed GPU runs, and 6 new 1000-step two-seed GPU runs across 6 arms testing Wiener-damped and unnormalized leverage key shrinkage plus causal row-leverage query gating): (1) Comparator-Specific & Descriptive Framing of Long-Horizon, Matched-Clock, and T=2048 Results (Section 1.2, Section 2.4 item 5, Section 3.3, Table 6, Section 4.1): Stated explicitly that against the accepted 1280-step gamma=0.98 recipe (2.00581 +/- 0.00199 Confirm: s42: 2.004409, s137: 2.007220), the 1255-step 1-draw arm (klev1_18calls, 2.00482 +/- 0.00687 Confirm) beats the 1235-step 4-draw arm (2.00687) on both seeds while showing mixed confirmation differences across seeds (-0.004440 on s42, +0.002460 on s137, mean -0.000990); noted at T=2048 that klev4 improves mean reused-test BPB by only 0.00018 over Banded-256 (with s42 2.017024 vs. 2.016957) while changing both gamma and key routing; and framed selective retrieval head formation after step 200 explicitly as a hypothesis. (2) Corrected Attribution to [16] v10 (Section 1.2 item 1, Section 4.1 item 3): Clarified that [16] v10's Proposition 6 Wiener-MMSE key filter operates inside its delayed zero-reverse-matrix-pullback learner (while separating local-pullback W_O^T u variants as diagnostic controls), explicitly listed active queries and keys (attn.c_q, attn.c_k) alongside its 6 dense matrix families in both Section 1.2 and Section 4.1, and quoted the general probe-count-dependent Wiener formula W_{tau,s}^{MMSE}(M) = M A_{tau,s}^2 / ((M-1)A_{tau,s}^2 + ||A_{tau,:}||_2^2). (3) Separate Stochastic Approximation & Conditional V-Mux Caching (Section 2.4 item 5, test_cowm_oe_and_antithetic_hubs.py): Framed vmux1_cached_lev_mmse as a separate stochastic approximation not characterized by Table 4D's clean-filter alignment numbers, made storing _cached_vmux_a_hat conditional on k_credit_mode == 'vmux1_cached_lev_mmse', and distinguished the recorded Milestone 12 resource measurements. (4) Cross-Destination Covariance in Transported Value-Credit Variance, CLI Modes, and Exact Experiment Counts (Section 1.2, Section 2.4 item 4, Section 4.2, README.md): Corrected Var(hat{u}_{v,t,c} | T_l) in Section 2.4(4) to sum_{s,r} gamma^{s+r-2t} T_{s,c} T_{r,c} Cov(hat{A}_{t,s}, hat{A}_{t,r}); added CLI aliases --mode milestone12_verify, --mode milestone12_vmux_cached, and --mode milestone13_{diag,pretrain200,pretrain1000,all}; and reconciled the exact JSON artifact count as 81 two-seed arms (162 seed runs across milestone2..13, including 10 two-seed arms / 20 seed runs in Milestone 12 and 6 two-seed arms / 12 seed runs in Milestone 13). (5) Milestone 13 Wiener-Damped & Unnormalized Leverage Key Shrinkage + Row-Leverage Query Gating (Section 2.4 item 5, Table 4D, Table 5B, Table 6): At step 50 (R=32), unnormalized linear leverage (kunnorm4_qlev, 4 ell_{s,tau}) and Wiener-damped leverage (kwienershrink4_qlev) lift plug-in cosine from 0.5704 to 0.6306 and 0.6496 (e2e cosine 0.003882 and 0.003801) and improve 200-step 18-call BPB from 2.07138 to 2.06786 +/- 0.00099; over 1000 steps, kunnorm4_qlev reaches 2.01170 +/- 0.00302 Confirm / 2.00754 +/- 0.00356 Reused Test (improving both seeds over gamma=0.98 and gamma=1.00 with lower inter-seed SD than klev4) and kwienershrink1_qlev_18calls (2.01526 +/- 0.00267 Confirm / 2.01265 +/- 0.00265 Reused Test) cuts inter-seed SD 2.6x vs. klev1_18calls (2.01096 +/- 0.00692), while unit-sum klev4 (2.01001) and klev1_18calls (2.01096) retain a slight 1000-step mean edge.
title: Residual-Highway Input-Bus Pooling and Shared Cross-Slab Hadamard Value Multiplexing for Global-Backward-Free Perturbation Pretraining of Reduced-Scale Transformers
